target_audience: Your target customers are logistics groups, energy companies and heavy industry, and leaders from each are in Formula 1: DHL (Formula 1), CEVA Logistics (Ferrari), bp (Audi) and Komatsu (Williams). market_reference: Zoox, your closest peer in autonomous driving, joined Williams in 2024 as an Official Regional Partner. Its logo runs on the car at US races, its robotaxi was shown at the team's Las Vegas fan zone, and it runs race-week activations in Austin and Miami.
shared_values: A Formula 1 team uses live data and software to make fast, safe decisions. Oxa does the same for industrial vehicles, with software that drives them safely at ports, airports and plants.
flags: Capacity: firm caution. Venture-backed and early in commercial revenue; Series D first close of 103m USD in March 2026 (UK National Wealth Fund 50m USD, NVentures, IP Group, Hostplus, bp Ventures).
Warm links, not partnerships: bp (Audi) is both an Oxa customer and an investor through bp Ventures; DHL (Formula 1) is a named customer.
Sectors dropped from target_audience: airports and ports (no verified grid example to cite). DHL Supply Chain, an Oxa customer, is quoted on oxa.tech about airport work at Heathrow.
Dubai joint venture SHIFFT is with Dubai Future Foundation, a Dubai government body; kept at mission level (no partner named in the email). First commercial deployment targeted before end of 2027.

A2RL (Abu Dhabi autonomous racing) in the chunk note is not F1; not used.
Zoox (Williams) is also the market reference in the EasyMile row.

target_audience: Your target customers are carmakers and their tier one suppliers, and leaders from each are in Formula 1: Ford (Red Bull), Toyota Gazoo Racing (Haas), Honda (Aston Martin) and MAHLE (Ferrari). B2B brands use the sport to host key clients, show their technology working under pressure and meet buyers worldwide. Teams also introduce partners to each other, to their owners and boards, and run joint activations at forums like CES and Web Summit.
market_overlap: ClearMotion builds in China for NIO, works with Porsche in Germany and has engineering teams in the US and the UK. The Formula 1 calendar aligns with the markets you are present in and expanding into: Shanghai, Silverstone, Miami, Austin and Las Vegas.
market_reference: Öhlins, the Brembo-owned suspension maker and your closest rival in performance ride control, became an official Ferrari Technical Partner in 2022 after years of engineering work with the team. Ferrari develops suspension with Öhlins, which gives it a technical reference at the top of the sport.
shared_values: A Formula 1 team controls how the car meets the road on every track. ClearMotion does this for road cars, with software that reads the road surface and active suspension that cancels unwanted body motion.
flags: Capacity: firm caution. Private, about 112 staff (PitchBook); one series production customer (NIO ET9, with the ES9 nominated for 2026), a 2024 Porsche cooperation and licence, and an unnamed second global automaker. Last reported raise 32m USD alongside the NIO order.
Active suspension is not allowed on F1 cars, so the deal would be a brand, hospitality and engineering partnership, not an on-car supply.

Öhlins was sold by Tenneco to Brembo (completed January 2025); Ferrari still lists Öhlins and Brembo as technical partners on RTR Sports' 2026 roster. Tenneco, maker of Monroe ride control, is Cadillac's Official Technical Partner from 2026, but that deal covers powertrain and ignition, so it is not used as the reference.
Investor link: NIO Capital led a 39m USD round in 2022; NIO is also the main customer. Plant in Changshu, China; office in Shanghai. Company HQ is US, so no China HQ override.
Porsche (customer) is not on the F1 grid; Audi (Audi) is in the same Volkswagen Group, a possible warm angle.

market_reference: Qualcomm, whose Snapdragon chips run car cockpits for the same carmakers you serve, has partnered with Mercedes since 2023. The Snapdragon logo runs on the car and the drivers' race suits, the team uses Qualcomm technology across its UK campus, and the deal builds fan experiences at races and online.
shared_values: A Formula 1 car runs on central computers and software that link every system. ECARX builds the central computers, cockpits and software that do this job in road cars, now in about 12 million vehicles.
flags: Capacity: soft note. Listed; 2026 revenue guidance 1.0 to 1.1bn USD reiterated in August 2026; Q2 2026 net loss narrowed to 12.0m USD; adjusted EBITDA positive for a fourth straight quarter; agreed to buy the Flyme software business (about 266m USD).

HQ override: China. ECARX lists London as headquarters (2025 20-F, Q2 2026 release), but it was founded in China in 2017, runs Chinese operations through PRC subsidiaries, and is controlled by Geely founder Li Shufu with Geely Holding as its key related-party customer.
Domain corrected: ecarx.com.cn does not resolve; the official site is ecarxgroup.com.

Screening: no match for ECARX on OpenSanctions (aggregates OFAC SDN, BIS Entity List and 1260H). Not state-owned. The US BIS connected-vehicle rule (final January 2025) restricts China-linked vehicle software in the US from model year 2027, so US races are left out of market_overlap.
State-owned customers: FAW Group appears among ECARX customer logos; not named in the email, mission-level only.
Warm angles, not partnerships: ECARX customer logos include Volkswagen (Audi team owner) and Mercedes-Benz (Mercedes team co-owner).

Market reference: Qualcomm is framed as a cockpit chip leader selling to the same carmakers, not as a rival, because ECARX may also use Qualcomm chips in some programs. Harman, a direct cockpit rival, left Ferrari before 2025.

market_reference: Aggreko, your direct competitor in mobile power and battery storage, became an Official Provider of Formula 1 in 2025. Its solar, battery and biofuel system powers the paddock at European races, a live showcase for every team and a reference customer aiming for net zero by 2030.
shared_values: Since 2026, Formula 1 power units take far more of their power from electricity. Xos helps fleets make the same shift, with electric trucks and mobile charging that work without waiting for grid upgrades.
flags: Capacity: hard caution. Repositioning: now describes itself as an energy storage and fleet electrification provider (Power Hub mobile battery launched June 2026; Xos Hub supported a hyperscaler data center build).

Defense and government: military bases, municipal fleets and school districts are listed target sectors, and Xos was a finalist at a US Air Force Global Strike Command showcase; mission-level only, not used in the email.
